explanation: Bone corresponds to frame: Bones in the skeletal system form the supporting structure of organisms; frames in architecture form the basic support of buildings. In this mapping, bones and frames are elements that provide support and stability for their respective systems.

Joints correspond to connectors: Joints in the skeletal system connect bones and allow movement; connectors in architecture connect various parts of the frame together. Here, joints and connectors are both parts responsible for connecting and enabling movement in their respective systems.

Muscles correspond to supporting structures: Muscles in the skeletal system provide strength and mobility to bones; supporting structures in architecture enhance the stability of buildings. In this mapping, muscles and supporting structures are elements that provide strength and stability for their respective systems.

Body corresponds to architecture: The skeletal system forms the basic framework of the body; architecture forms the basic framework of buildings. Here, body and architecture are both the overall structures of their respective systems.

background.source: The skeletal system is the internal framework of the body that provides support and structure. Composed of bones, joints, and muscles, it is responsible for movement, protection of internal organs, and the production of red and white blood cells. The skeleton is categorized into exoskeleton, endoskeleton, and hydroskeleton, depending on the type of organism. Vertebrates have an endoskeleton made up of bone and cartilage surrounding the spinal column, while invertebrates have a variety of skeletal systems depending on their species. Regardless of the type, the skeletal system is essential for maintaining the shape and function of the body.
background.target: Building structures are essential components of modern architecture, providing support and stability to the world's tallest and most impressive structures. The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands as the world's tallest self-supported building, with a height of 2,717 feet, while the Tokyo Skytree is the highest tower. Meanwhile, the KVLY-TV mast represents the tallest guyed structure, standing at a height of 1,987 feet. While there are various structures that surpass the height of the world's tallest buildings, only those with at least 49% habitable floor area are officially recognized. The construction of such impressive buildings requires a sturdy supporting structure, efficient connectors, and a reliable frame. These architectural features are essential in ensuring the safety and stability of the structure, and every component must be carefully integrated to create a functional and aesthetic masterpiece.
